item.title: Jonathan Taylor delivers what sounds like a goodbye to Indianapolis after Colts' fifth straight loss
item.description: Jonathan Taylor delivered an emotional postgame message that sounded like a goodbye to Indianapolis as the NFL trade deadline looms Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Jonathan Taylor is done watching the Colts shoot themselves in the foot. Sunday's 27-23 loss to Dallas dropped Indy to an ugly 2-7, cementing their fifth straight defeat.

As the lone Pro Bowl weapon on a broken offense, the franchise running back has outgrown the dysfunction. And he can read the situation clearly.

With Tuesday's trade deadline looming and this Colts team firmly in fire-sale territory, Taylor didn't bother feeding reporters the company line at the podium, delivering what sounded an awful lot like a parting goodbye to Indy.

JONATHAN TAYLOR ADDRESSES TRADE RUMORS AMID COLTS' FIRE SALE: 'HOPEFULLY THAT DAY MAY NOT COME'

"I think you play every game like it's your last, but at the end of the day this has been a spot where I grew up," Taylor said.

JONATHAN TAYLOR'S WIFE KNOWS THINGS SO DIRE FAMILY IS ON 'COLTS TRANSACTION WATCH' EXPECTING TRADES OR FIRING

"I think I mentioned this to you guys, like you go to college, you're a young man, but you really grew up, you started a family and you really embraced this city, the people, and you're just like ... this place helped shape me into the man I am today. If it is [my last game], I'm very grateful for the city of Indianapolis."

Taylor continued, "I just hope that they appreciate and know that I appreciate them and it was a pleasure to put on display not only my hard work but the team's hard work each and every single week, each and every single year. Just know it was a pleasure."

Before Sunday's kickoff, Fox NFL Insider Jay Glazer reported that the team hottest on Taylor's trail, the New York Giants, pulled their trade proposal. New York had put a second- and fifth-round pick package on the table with extra compensation, but backed off after the Colts held out for a first-rounder. That steep asking price remains the sticking point, but other contenders like Denver and Cincinnati are lingering — both clubs could use a premier bell-cow back to supercharge a postseason run.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The three-time Pro Bowler already took home the NFL rushing crown in 2021 with over 1,800 yards and 18 touchdowns, and he delivered another monster campaign in 2025 with nearly 1,600 yards on the ground.

The Colts already fired GM Chris Ballard and shipped off locker room leaders Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner for future draft capital. Taylor remains under contract through 2028, giving Indy leverage.

Unless the front office lowers its demands before Tuesday's 4 p.m. (ET) cutoff, Taylor will stay trapped in Indianapolis, carrying an offense that cannot stop beating itself.

item.title: Bernie Sanders warns Democrats not to spend all their time investigating Trump
item.description: Sen. Bernie Sanders warned Democrats not to spend all their time investigating the Trump administration, urging the party to prioritize affordability and working-class families.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Bernie Sanders said Democrats should hold President Donald Trump accountable after taking control of the House and Senate in January, but warned the party not to spend too much time on probing the president and his allies.

During an appearance on NBC News' "Meet the Press," the senator said it is still important to investigate Trump administration officials for alleged corruption and illegal activity, but stressed that the priority should be tackling affordability and supporting working-class families.

Asked by host Kristen Welker if he believes that spending two years investigating Trump and his officials could jeopardize the mandate to lower prices and make life more affordable, Sanders replied, "Yes, I do."

"Do we want to hold the Trump administration accountable for their corruption, for their illegal, unconstitutional actions? Absolutely," Sanders said.

DEMS PIVOT FROM ‘AFFORDABILITY’ PITCH TO DHS PROBE THREATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS

However, Sanders said that Democrats "cannot spend all of our time investigating Trump."

"At the end of the day, when you’ve got the highest rate of childhood poverty in America, of any major country, when 20% of our seniors are trying to survive on $15,000 a year, when people are scared to death that Elon Musk and the other billionaires are pushing AI down our throats with cataclysmic impacts on the economy, our privacy rights, on our health, and — and imposing an existential threat to humanity, we cannot spend all of our time investigating Trump," he said.

"We’ve got to stand up for working-class families, make a real difference in their lives," Sanders continued.

Democrats campaigned on affordability ahead of the midterms, blaming the Trump administration for the soaring costs of gas, groceries, housing and healthcare. Candidates linked the rise in costs, in part, to the U.S. military's war on Iran and Trump's tariffs on countries around the world.

The Iran war, which Trump, Vice President JD Vance and other allies partially attributed to Republicans' midterm losses, led to surging fuel prices. Gas prices are nearly $1 per gallon higher than they were a year ago, according to AAA, which reported that the national average was $4.02 per gallon as of Sunday.

But after securing the majority in both chambers of Congress following last week's elections, several Democrats promised to use the power of the subpoena and investigate current and former Trump officials once they are sworn in.

‘LAWYER UP’: DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

Incoming House Oversight Committee leader Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., on Sunday warned that Democrats could investigate Trump's pardons as well as allies of the president, including tech executive Elon Musk and newly appointed White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.

Garcia also said last week that Oversight Democrats are "ready to take on the crooks, the con men, and the Trump crime family."

"Lawyer up," he added.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., who is expected to be the next House Speaker, also said last week that Democrats are "going to bring accountability to those who have visited unprecedented corruption on this country."

"Because if you have people in high office who are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends or their donors, then they’re not focused on making life better for the American people. But House Democrats will put the American people first," he continued.

Sanders said on Sunday that the election was not just about voters wanting to stop the Trump administration’s policies.

"What I think this election was about, is the American people not only expressing disgust with Trump and his policies, but are demanding real change, no more tinkering around the edges," said Sanders. "And what the American people are saying: 'Look, we are working long hours. We’re worried about our kids. We can’t afford healthcare. We can’t afford housing. Meanwhile, the wealthiest people in America have never, ever had it so good.' And right now is the moment where the Democrats have got to stand up to big money, create an economy and a government that works for all of us," Sanders said.

The Vermont senator also accused Trump of being "mentally unbalanced" and "erratic," but acknowledged that the president is "a good politician" and "not stupid" who Democrats may be able to work with on economic and healthcare issues.

"Trump is many things. I personally believe he is mentally unbalanced, erratic, but he’s not stupid, and he is a good politician. And I think, when Trump looks out in the world and he sees millions of people working for starvation wages, he might not be unsympathetic to raising the minimum wage to a living wage. He would love, I think, to take credit for doing what every other major country does, guaranteeing healthcare to all people. Do I think we can work with Trump? Maybe. I’m, by no means, guaranteeing it. But it is certainly worth the effort," he said.

item.title: Two Washington deputies killed trying to rescue possible hostages after woman shot
item.description: Two Washington state sheriff's deputies were fatally shot responding to a domestic violence call near Spangle as they tried to rescue potential hostages.
item.content:encoded:
Two Washington state sheriff’s deputies were fatally shot as they moved in to rescue possible hostages after a woman called for help following a domestic violence shooting, according to authorities. 

Spokane County Sheriff’s Deputies Mason Acheson and Parker Perry came under fire from inside the home near Spangle, south of Spokane, as they tried to get in on Nov. 3, the sheriff’s office said.

The Spokane County Sheriff’s Office and Spokane Valley Police Department said they were devastated by the shooting and pledged to support the deputies’ families.

YOUNG SOUTH DAKOTA DEPUTY DIES THREE DAYS AFTER BEING SHOT DURING A CONFRONTATION AT A HOME

"They bravely moved toward danger to protect others they did not know," the agencies said in a statement. "They are true examples of selfless service and dedication."

Deputies first responded around 2:25 p.m. after a woman reported she had been shot.

SOUTH CAROLINA POLICE OFFICER KILLED, ANOTHER WOUNDED IN GUNFIGHT WITH SUSPECT WHO HAD EXTENSIVE RECORD

The sheriff’s office said they learned the suspect had an active felony warrant and might have access to more weapons. With other victims possibly still inside, they called in SWAT. The woman was taken to the hospital with injuries that appeared to be non-life-threatening.

Perry, a K-9 deputy, answered the call with his dog, Brego. He joined the team approaching the house around 3:15 p.m. and forced his way in, the sheriff’s office said.

AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND

When gunfire struck Perry and Acheson, their teammates fired back, pulled them to cover and began treating their wounds. Authorities called for medical helicopters and closed stretches of Interstate 90 and U.S. Highway 195 to help get the deputies to the hospital, the Washington State Patrol said.

Acheson died after being taken to the hospital. Perry remained on life support while arrangements were made for him to donate his organs. The sheriff’s office said he would "continue to serve others with the gift of life." Both men left behind wives and two children. Perry and his wife were expecting their third.

WATCH: EVICTION STANDOFF TURNS TO WAR ZONE AS GUNMAN KILLS DEPUTY IN AMBUSH, GETS RUN OVER BY ARMORED VEHICLE

Back at the house, Spokane police took over the scene after SWAT teams from Spokane and Kootenai County were called in. A drone sent inside found the suspect dead, the State Patrol said.

The Spokane County medical examiner determined that Ryan Larsen, 37, died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound, The Spokesman-Review reported. The medical examiner also identified two other people killed as Suzanne Larsen, 72, and Rebecca Larsen, 45. A family obituary identified them as Larsen’s mother and sister, according to the newspaper.

"It was a very tragic day in Spokane County," Sheriff John Nowels told reporters, according to the outlet. "A lot of families have been affected."

Acheson and Perry served in the same Washington Army National Guard infantry battalion, the sheriff's office shared. Acheson enlisted in 2011, rose to sergeant and served in Poland from 2021 to 2022, earning three Army Commendation Medals during his military service. He spent eight years as a Washington State Patrol trooper and firearms instructor before joining the sheriff’s office in 2022. As a SWAT sniper, he watched over teammates as they went into dangerous scenes.

AS AN ARMY WIDOW, I WILL NEVER FORGET HOW ORDINARY AMERICANS HONORED MY HUSBAND

"In the face of danger, he stepped forward to preserve life," the sheriff’s office said of Acheson.

Perry joined the sheriff’s office in 2020 and spent three years on its SWAT team before becoming a K-9 deputy in 2025. He joined the Guard in 2017, rose to captain as a military intelligence officer and earned two Army Commendation Medals. When the call came in near Spangle, he responded "on his own, without prompting," the sheriff’s office said.

PHILLY OFFICER MURDERED IN LINE OF DUTY PROMOTED TO SERGEANT AS POLICE FROM AROUND US ATTEND HIS FUNERAL

FBI Director Kash Patel honored each deputy in a separate post on X, listing Nov. 4 as Acheson’s end of watch and Nov. 7 as Perry’s.

Patel noted that both men were military veterans and pledged the bureau’s support to their families, friends and colleagues. "They will have our full support," he wrote in both posts.

The FBI also issued separate tributes to Acheson and Perry.

Rep. Michael Baumgartner, R-Wash., said he knew Acheson and his wife from a CrossFit gym and that she was his children’s first piano teacher. "Just wonderful people," he wrote in one tribute.

In another post, Baumgartner asked people to keep both families in their prayers and said the deputies "both died protecting our community."

Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson ordered flags at state facilities lowered to half-staff Monday, Nov. 9, in the deputies’ honor.

The Spokane County Sheriff’s Office said the Sheriff Community Oriented Policing Effort is accepting donations to help cover the deputies’ funeral expenses, with any remaining funds going to their families. The sheriff’s office said it was "grateful and honored by the outpouring of heartfelt condolences and prayers."

"The families have requested privacy as they suffer this enormous loss," the sheriff’s office said.

item.title: Giants star wideout blasts analyst for questioning sideline behavior during win against Eagles
item.description: Malik Nabers fired back at Greg Olsen on Instagram after the Fox analyst questioned his sideline frustration during the Giants' win over the Eagles.
item.content:encoded:
Win or lose, Malik Naberswill always make sure he gets the last word.

The New York Giants snapped a 13-game skid in Philly on Sunday, grinding through a 19-11 clunker featuring backup versus backup-backup quarterbacks. But as New York closed in on a rare division road win, Nabers — the Giants' star wideout — spent parts of the game pacing away from the huddle, shaking his head in plain view of the cameras.

Fox analyst Greg Olsen spotted Nabers' bad body language on the sideline and called it out during the live broadcast.

"It's not good," he said, "there's a fine line between being demanding and chasing greatness and then being a bad teammate … like if your teammate scores a touchdown for the lead and you're still worried about your touches."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

After the win, Nabers went straight to Instagram postgame.

He said, in part: "[Olsen] calling me a bad teammate when every team I've been on, there's NOBODY I've played with has said dat bout me is crazy! Y'all be trying to create a narrative on me soo bad it's actually crazy!! If you [don't] like the way I play the game, keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE!"

KANSAS CITY CHIEFS STAR DEFENSIVE LINEMAN CHRIS JONES CAUGHT IN SCREAMING MATCH WITH COACHES ON SIDELINES

In reality, Nabers had a dud and couldn't hide it. Against a shaky Eagles secondary, he finished with five catches for 43 yards and dropped a walk-in fourth-quarter touchdown from J.J. McCarthy.

Olsen didn't sugarcoat anything, and he didn't have to. Nabers has All-Pro ability, but the diva act and injury baggage are getting impossible to ignore.

Back in November 2024, Nabers openly slammed the offense after seeing zero targets until the game was out of reach. In Week 1 last season, he was back in Brian Daboll's ear on the sideline complaining about touches. Three weeks later, his sophomore year was over with a torn ACL and meniscus against the Chargers.

A dominant October buys goodwill, and 509 receiving yards through a quarterback carousel is legitimately impressive. But getting rattled by a television broadcast only proves the critique right.

The 5-2-1 Giants host the Commanders on Thursday night.

item.title: Trump says he doesn’t disagree with Vance that Iran war fueled GOP losses
item.description: President Donald Trump said he doesn’t disagree with JD Vance’s assessment that the Iran war, rising costs and Israel ties contributed to GOP midterm losses.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Sunday said he does not disagree with Vice President JD Vance's assessment that the Republicans' sweeping midterm losses were caused by the Iran war, rising costs and U.S. relations with Israel.

"I don’t disagree with it," Trump said during a CBS 60 Minutes interview.

Asked whether he knew Vance was planning to share his take in a post on X, Trump said the vice president was fully transparent with him beforehand

"He asked me what do I think," Trump said.

VANCE'S SCATHING IRAN WAR POSTMORTEM PUTS POTENTIAL 2028 GOP SHOWDOWN IN FOCUS: 'EVERYONE KNOWS WHY'

"I said, ‘You write what you want. By the way, what are you going to write?’"

Trump added that the one thing he wished Vance would have done differently was share whether the vice president would have made the decision to strike Iran again, given his role in the administration's decision-making process.

"The only thing I wish he would've said there, if he felt it," Trump said.

"My answer is an emphatic yes, because you can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," Trump said.

He said the administration's decision to engage in war with Iran was far more important than the political consequences of losing the midterm elections, arguing that while the decision may be unpopular, the alternative would have been allowing Tehran to obtain a nuclear weapon.

"I think, historically, this will be a very good decision. Is it a good decision for today and tomorrow? Maybe not," he said.

"I have to go with what's right for our country. If they had a nuclear weapon during my term, I would be excoriated far worse than what's happened."

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

On Wednesday, Vance delivered a blunt assessment of Republicans' midterm losses, which allowed Democrats to regain control of both chambers of Congress in a major blow to the Trump administration. Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts.

"The real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone," Vance wrote on X. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night."

Like Trump, Vance argued that the political consequences of the war were a "worthwhile cost to pay."

"If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so," Vance said. "Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost."

item.title: Trump admits immigration enforcement may have been too 'tough' in first interview since midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump conceded his deportation policies may have been too "tough" and suggested that he could make a deal with the incoming Democratic Congress.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump admitted that he may have been too "tough" in his immigration enforcement in his first sit-down interview since the midterm elections last week.

Trump spoke to CBS News correspondent Ross Douthat about several topics largely related to the Democratic Party's overwhelming wins in last week's midterm elections, which included victories in Republican strongholds like Texas.

During their conversation, Douthat asked whether Trump's strict immigration and deportation enforcement likely contributed to Republican losses.

CONSERVATIVES STUNNED BY 'CATASTROPHIC' MIDTERM BLUE TSUNAMI, BLAME TRUMP'S IRAN WAR, HIGH GAS PRICES

"I think it both helped and hurt," Trump answered. "I think I got an A-plus for closing up the border…I get very high marks for getting the bad ones out."

In the extended interview posted online, Trump added, "We had 25 million people come in through Biden over a four-year period, and many of those people were — as you know, they were from prisons, they were drug dealers, they were from mental institutions."

However, Trump conceded that many illegal immigrants within the country were "good" people, which likely led to his policies facing backlash.

"But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that — that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally. Now, there is a large part of the country that think that they should be put out. And there's a large part of the country that think that they should be allowed to stay if they're good people working in a landscaping company, or working in a hotel, or doing something, right? And in some cases, paying taxes. And there's a large group of people who think that they should be allowed to stay."

FLORIDA CONGRESSMAN DIAGNOSES GOP'S BLUE TSUNAMI LOSSES: 'WE FAILED TO MAKE THEM THINK WE CARED ABOUT THEM'

"So you think your deportation policy — went too far?" Douthat asked.

"I think it was — too tough…I think it might be too tough, yeah," Trump responded, adding, "And I think ultimately that hurt me."

The president also suggested an immigration deal with the incoming Democratic Congress could be "doable" outside the more extreme groups who either prefer every illegal immigrant to be deported or prefer not to deport any illegal immigrant.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Trump also suggested many Democrats are willing to work with him to enforce the border, acknowledging incoming Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico as an example.

In a Fox News voter poll of more than 100,000 registered voters nationwide from Oct. 19 to Nov. 3, 2026, immigration was the only issue that Republicans led Democrats on.

item.title: Dallas public defender’s chief investigator charged with wife’s murder after bloody apartment discovery
item.description: Jimmy Spurger Jr., a Dallas County capital murder investigator, is accused of stabbing his wife Maria just days after filing divorce papers.
item.content:encoded:
A Texas investigator who spent years working on capital murder cases is now accused of killing his wife of roughly 35 years, less than two weeks after filing for divorce.

Jimmy Spurger Jr., 54, the chief investigator for the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office, faces a first-degree felony murder charge after his wife, Maria Spurger, was found stabbed to death inside their downtown Dallas apartment Friday night.

Emergency crews found Maria on a couch with a knife in her neck and her husband sitting on a bed in another room, covered in blood, according to an arrest affidavit obtained by Fox 4 Dallas.

Spurger filed for divorce Oct. 26, less than two weeks before the killing, according to Dallas County court records. The case was still open, with a Nov. 3 entry indicating Maria had not been served with the divorce papers.

TEACHER FOUND DEAD WITH THROAT SLIT; DETECTIVES SCRUTINIZE HUSBAND’S SHIFTING STORY

Dallas County Judge Clay Lewis Jenkins said Sunday that he had ordered Spurger suspended and his access revoked.

"Upon notice of this tragic murder yesterday, I instructed Administration to place the employee on suspension and remove his access," Jenkins wrote on X.

Firefighters received a welfare check call around 10:40 p.m. Friday and went to the couple’s apartment on North Akard Street, according to the affidavit.

No one answered their repeated knocks. When firefighters forced the door open, they found furniture blocking the entrance.

They moved it aside and found Maria unresponsive on the couch. Spurger was sitting on a bed in the bedroom, but he did not answer when firefighters asked whether he was OK.

The crews backed out and called police.

Officers arrived around 11:13 p.m. and found Spurger covered in blood, with a small knife beside him. Several empty pill bottles covered in blood were in the kitchen, according to the affidavit. No one else was found inside.

IVY LEAGUE-EDUCATED PEDIATRICIAN ALLEGEDLY MURDERED BY HUSBAND WHO THEN SET HOME ON FIRE: POLICE

Maria was pronounced dead at the apartment. Spurger was taken to Methodist Central Hospital, and investigators said they could not interview him because he may have taken multiple pills.

He was booked into the Dallas County Jail Saturday on a murder charge and is being held without bond, according to jail records.

RETIRED POLICE SERGEANT SHOOTS DEPUTY CHIEF WIFE AND THEIR DAUGHTER IN WEALTHY, COASTAL ENCLAVE HOME

Before his arrest, Spurger oversaw investigators who helped public defenders prepare criminal cases, according to the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office website. His biography says he served as chief investigator for 11 months.

He spent more than 13 years with the office, primarily in its Capital Murder Division, where his work included examining evidence and interviewing witnesses.

FORMER CORRECTIONS OFFICER ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE, FORCING KIDS TO HELP

Before joining the public defender’s office, Spurger spent more than 20 years in law enforcement, specializing in homicide investigations and crimes against people, according to the website. During his final decade in law enforcement, he supervised child abuse and family violence investigations for the Dallas County District Attorney’s Office.

Police have not released a motive and said the killing remains under investigation.

Anyone with information is asked to contact Detective C. Johnson at 214-671-3584 or chanesia.johnson@dallaspolice.gov.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Dallas Police Department for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Tensions flare as demonstrators target Jewish restaurants, drawing massive counterprotest
item.description: The demonstration targeted six restaurants in Philadelphia’s Rittenhouse Square as Jewish and pro-Israel groups organized a counterprotest.
item.content:encoded:
Tensions flared in a Philadelphia neighborhood Sunday after a bike ride organized to boycott several Jewish-owned restaurants sparked overwhelming backlash from the city's Jewish and pro-Israel communities.

The "boycott ride" targeted at least six restaurants in Philadelphia's Rittenhouse Square, labeling them "Zionist establishments" and calling for them to leave, according to pro-Palestinian group Philly Bike On Your Left, which organized the event.

As riders cycled through the streets waving Palestinian flags, hundreds of Jewish and pro-Israel community members turned out to oppose the demonstration, with heated exchanges unfolding across several city blocks. Dozens of diners also lined up outside the targeted restaurants in a show of solidarity with the Jewish-owned businesses.

The boycott also drew sharp criticism for taking place on the eve of the anniversary of Kristallnacht, the 1938 Nazi pogrom against Jews in Germany and Austria marked by widespread anti-Jewish violence, including attacks on homes, synagogues and businesses.

PHILADELPHIA 'BOYCOTT RIDE' TARGETING JEWISH BUSINESSES DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM CITY, STATE LEADERSHIP

The Philadelphia police told Fox News that at least three people were arrested in connection with the protest, including a woman accused of assault, a man accused of disorderly conduct and a 17-year-old male accused of assaulting police.

Meanwhile, a female counterprotester reported being assaulted by an unknown individual.

Two officers also sustained minor injuries during the arrest of one individual, according to the outlet. Neither required medical treatment.

No property damage was reported, and conditions returned to normal by late afternoon, police said. 

Police said about 500 people participated in total, including roughly 300 pro-Palestinian demonstrators, 200 of whom were on bicycles, and 200 pro-Israeli counterprotesters.

ANTI-ISRAEL AGITATORS CLASH WITH NYPD OFFICERS NEAR SYNAGOGUE

Videos circulating on social media showed demonstrators and counterprotesters shouting at one another.

In one video, a restaurant displayed a Palestinian flag alongside a sign reading "No public restroom" on its entrance door.

A man confronted the restaurant on camera, accusing it of sending a message that the Jewish community was not welcome.

The protest, organized in late October, targeted six businesses whose owners organizers accused of being "Zionist business owners."

"We see them for the disgusting humans they are," the group said. 

"There are business owners in our community who have raised funds for the Israeli military, hosted Israeli soldiers, were praised by Benjamin Netanyahu, or expressed support for Israel," the group added.

The demonstration prompted the Jewish Federation of Greater Philadelphia to call for a counter-demonstration in early November.

GERMAN OFFICIALS WARN ISLAMIST, FAR-LEFT RHETORIC DRIVING SPIKE IN ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS

"This is antisemitism. It is Jew-Hatred, plain and simple," the organization said.

"The ride falls on the eve of the anniversary of Kristallnacht, November 9-10, 1938, when Nazi-organized mobs destroyed thousands of Jewish businesses, homes and synagogues in Germany and Austria, while thousands of Jews were beaten, assaulted and sent to concentration camps. The public targeting of Jewish businesses should alarm every person of conscience. We cannot allow such hatred to become normalized in Philadelphia."

The organizers, however, pushed back against the criticism, claiming their ride had been "grossly misrepresented" and describing themselves as a nonviolent social cycling group.

item.title: Donna Mills on why she never married despite decades-long romance: 'I was always so independent'
item.description: Donna Mills reveals why she and Larry Gilman never married despite 25 years together, citing her fierce independence and a practical approach to love.
item.content:encoded:
"Knots Landing" star Donna Mills is revealing the reason that she has never walked down the aisle despite her 25-year romance with actor Larry Gilman.

During a recent appearance on the "Still Here Hollywood Podcast with Steve Kmetko," the 85-year-old actress, who has been in a relationship with Gilman, 76, since 2001, opened up about why she has chosen to avoid marriage.

"I was always so independent," she told Kmetko. "I’m still very independent."

RITA WILSON IGNORED HER MOTHER'S OLD-SCHOOL MARRIAGE ADVICE, AND IT LED HER TO TOM HANKS

"I just didn’t ever want to be subject to whatever you have to do when you get married," Mills continued. "I also didn’t want to say I was going to love somebody forever."

"I don’t know if I would do that or not," she admitted with a laugh.

‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH LIVED APART FROM HER HUSBAND FOR 17 YEARS DURING THEIR 35-YEAR LOVE STORY

Mills shared the topic of marriage had also come up between herself and her daughter Chloe, who recently tied the knot herself.

"It’s funny because my daughter asked me that. My daughter just got married," Mills said. "And she just had a baby."

After Kmetko told her that she didn't "look like a grandmother," Mills pointed to a necklace she was wearing that was inscribed with the word "Grandma," which she said was a gift from Chloe.

"She gave me this, and I wear it all the time," Mills said.

Mills explained that she and Chloe have had many conversations about what name her grandson would call her.

"And I said, "'Oh, I know. Glamma,'" Mills told Kmetko with a laugh. "But she didn't like that."

The Daytime Emmy Award winner Chloe adopted as a newborn in 1994 when she was 54. Seven years later, Mills began dating Gilman, whom she has described as an "incredibly kind, funny, wonderful man."

"I love him," she told The Daily Beast in 2022. "I’m lucky to have found him. I found him late, but I found him. Everybody loves him. He’s great."

NICOLE KIDMAN, RACHAEL RAY, TED DANSON KEEP MARRIAGES HOT WITH UNCONVENTIONAL RULES

Prior to meeting Gilman, Mills and advertising executive Richard Holland, who was previously married to singer Chaka Khan, had an on-and-off relationship for around 20 years starting in 1979.

When asked why she has never married, Mills said, "I don’t remember anyone ever getting down on one knee."

TIM MCGRAW WARNS OF ‘MOST DANGEROUS’ TIMES IN MARRIAGE AFTER 30 YEARS WITH FAITH HILL

The "Nope" star also cited her independent streak and explained why she and Gilman never felt the need to marry after meeting later in life.

"I am so freaking independent. I just am. I’m very independent and by the time Larry and I met we were both pretty established," she said. "To combine everything at that point is really difficult. So we just combined our lives but not our finances and stuff like that. It’s much cleaner, much better."

GREAT RELATIONSHIPS HAVE 3 ESSENTIAL INGREDIENTS — AND ONE FACTOR THAT CAN RUIN EVERYTHING

Mills shared that maintaining her independence had always given her a sense of security, even while sharing her life with a partner.

"I’ve always felt a woman being independent was important," she said. "It made me feel safer, I guess, to know that I can take care of myself. I want someone to be in my life to love and be with, to be a companion and to go places and all that, but if I have to I can take care of myself."

item.title: Will College Football Playoff committee drop LSU Tigers out of playoff picture after blowout loss?
item.description: Lane Kiffin's SEC propaganda campaign paid off as the first College Football Playoff poll overranked conference teams, sparking outrage from rivals.
item.content:encoded:
The release of the first College Football Playoff poll recently was treated with shock, disdain, and outright anger from many fans across the sport. Unless they root for the SEC.

SEC teams were shockingly, and consistently overrepresented and overranked, to the point that prominent rival coaches openly speculated about a connection between ESPN, the SEC, and the committee's willingness to abandon any pretense of objectivity.

Defending national champion Curt Cignetti, as one example, was blunt about his perception of the committee's bias.

TIM BRANDO JOINS DAN DAKICH ON 'DON'T @ ME' TO DISCUSS INDIANA COACH CURT CIGNETTI'S CFP 'BIAS' COMMENTS

"SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN and all their writers that they don't technically pay but march to their drum," he said. "That's why you see all these SEC teams up there, and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten not quite as high. But like I said, it's all going to be played out on the field."

"Come on. These people, and there’s a whole bunch of them, they march out of the tent, and they’re given instructions on what to say," he added. "And they follow the company line. Right, and I don’t need to go any further."

There's little doubt that the SEC's marketing efforts have been extremely effective at ensuring voters ignore results and focus on perception instead. And the biggest winner might have been the conference's most effective marketer: LSU Tigers head coach Lane Kiffin.

Kiffin has been loudly decrying the conference's move to nine games, correctly realizing that the extra losses , which put the SEC on equal footing with the Big Ten and Big 12, will be tough to overcome when evaluating resumes. To combat this, he's spent most of the past year campaigning for the benefit of the committee. Saying, incorrectly, that the SEC is Just Different and deserves to be treated like special snowflakes relative to other conferences.

"The conferences are so different," he said recently. "They are. They’re different stadiums, they’re different environments, they’re different middle to bottom of them. So you’re not playing equal schedules, they’re not even close. If you took an SEC team and gave them another one of those conference’s schedules, they’d average two more wins. Well, that’s a big deal. So, I say all that to say you had to go to more teams, because the system’s broke in how they pick them."

Pretty much all of that is wrong. But his propaganda efforts, based on the first week's poll, clearly worked. Losses in the SEC simply don't matter as much as they should, a trend that was obvious in 2025 when the Alabama Crimson Tide were blown out by Georgia in the conference championship game and didn't drop a single spot. The committee decided ahead of time that they should be in, so they determined that the SEC Championship Game could only help the winner, and not hurt the loser.

Will that same preferential treatment be given to the loser of a, say, Utah-BYU Big 12 Championship Game? Of course not. Because of the stadiums or something. Returning to Kiffin's diatribe though, one stat that he curiously never brings up is the SEC's recent performance when the games actually matter. And unfortunately for him and them, it's not very good.

In 2025-2026, the SEC went 1-8 in bowl games. They were 0-3 in the College Football Playoff against non-SEC P4 opponents. Texas A&M went 7-1 in the SEC and was a tiebreaker away from reaching the conference championship game, then scored all of three points against a lowly Miami Hurricanes team at home. In their awe-inspiring temple of an SEC stadium.

Houston beat LSU in their bowl game. Virginia beat Missouri. Illinois beat Tennessee. Iowa beat Vanderbilt. Then Alabama, the team gifted a spot in the playoff thanks to their conference patch, was obliterated by Indiana 38-3 in the Rose Bowl. So two of the top three teams in the SEC, Texas A&M and Alabama, lost their non-SEC playoff games by a combined score of 48-6. Six points combined.

"They're not even close." "They'd average two more wins." And people actually believe this stuff.

Since the expanded playoff format started, SEC teams are 2-5 against other P4 conference teams. They're 5-7 overall, while the Big Ten is 8-5. "They're not even close."

There's another part of Kiffin's ridiculous posturing that he never brings up: travel. This isn't the SEC's fault, of course, but the conference's geographic alignment gives them a tremendous advantage over the Big Ten or ACC. LSU is in the Central Time Zone. Of their 12 games, just two were or are scheduled for any other time zone, Kentucky and Tennessee. They already lost to the Wildcats.

USC, by contrast, plays four games in other time zones, including three in the Eastern Time Zone. USC, despite being based in Los Angeles, plays more times in the Eastern Time Zone than LSU does. UCLA has six games in time zones other than its home Pacific time zone. That's a massive advantage for the Tigers and for most SEC teams. Their travel schedules simply don't match up to the grueling gauntlet of the Big Ten. Just imagine how many more losses Kiffin and his marketing group would have if they had to travel like their peers. But stadiums or something.

This isn't the first time the SEC boosters have done their fake superiority performance. And yet they learn nothing from it.

December 2024 - Lane Kiffin: "The SEC is just different, it's totally different. You might as well be in different leagues, not different conferences, different leagues."

June 2025 - Vanderbilt QB Diego Pavia: "You want to play with the best — you don’t want to play with the Big Ten. … You ignore those calls."

July 2025 - Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko: "It’s a gauntlet going into the SEC season."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

October 2025 - Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer: "This is our third game in a row in the conference against a ranked opponent. That’s life in the SEC."

October 2025 - Paul Finebaum: "I’d like to see Indiana go through the gauntlet that Alabama has gone through…"

November 2025 - Lane Kiffin: "Texas A&M being [No.] 3 — what more do you want them to do to be [No.] 1?"

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

December 2025 - SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey: "I actually think we deserve seven in," he said referring to the number of SEC teams that should be in the playoff. "I think the seven teams that are in the top-14, half of the top 14 teams are from the SEC. That's an indication that this league is different, the expectations are different, the competition is different, and the rewards should respect each of those elements."

December 2025 - Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea: "This should be about the 12 best teams in the country and a 10-2 team in the SEC … look, obviously we love our league. It just means more here and all that kind of stuff, but there’s a level of respect that needs to be held for the gauntlet we’ve been through and how we’ve met the match and done the things we need to do," Lea told OutKick. "I mean, it is just absurd the idea that we’re going to open the door to teams that play in conferences that aren’t the SEC that have the same record we have. I mean, it’s crazy."

December 2025 - Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian: "If you really look at the body of work, and you look at the Southeastern Conference of what we have to go through every week, you look at the non-conference schedule we played, to go to Ohio State in Week 1 and lose by seven when we outgained them by nearly 200 yards—we got a really good football team. It would be a disservice to our sport if this team is not a playoff team when we went and scheduled that non-conference game."

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

December 2025 - Alabama QB Ty Simpson: "In general, we think that... actually we know we have the best offense in the country."

This is why it's so galling that the committee listened to Kiffin and Sankey and Sark and the relentless propaganda: it's just wrong. It's been proven wrong. It is not accurate.

Kiffin's Tigers were blown out by Alabama on Saturday night, to the point where their awe-inspiring stadium was mostly empty halfway through the fourth quarter. Will the committee keep them without shouting distance of the top-12? Or will they do what they would to another team and conference, and drop the Tigers to the bottom of the top 25 or out of it entirely?

This is why Kiffin made these comments, because he hoped that the standards will be lower for him than they are for other schools. Lose three times? It's because of stadiums or some nonsense. Lose four times? It's because of Nick Saban in 2015. There can never be consequences for the SEC, because they're just special.

Kiffin's right, the system they use to select teams is broken. We'll just have to see how broken, in his favor, it actually is.

item.title: Joe Biden says cancer slowed him down, limiting memoir promotion tour
item.description: Former President Joe Biden revealed his prostate cancer battle will limit promotional events for his presidential memoir, "Promise Me, America," out Nov. 17.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden said on Sunday ahead of the release of his presidential memoir that he would need to limit the promotional events due to his cancer battle slowing him down at times.

The memoir, titled "Promise Me, America," is set to be released on Nov. 17. The book reflects on Biden's four years in the White House, covering the COVID-19 pandemic, the aftermath of the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot, domestic legislation, global diplomacy and his decision to run for re-election before later stepping aside in 2024. The memoir also details the personal deliberations behind his decision to end his 2024 re-election bid.

"My presidential memoir, PROMISE ME, AMERICA, is coming out on November 17th. I hope you'll read it. It covers my years as President. The challenges we faced, the decisions I made, and why I made them. It's about who we are as a nation. What we stand for. And America's role in the world. More than anything, it's about my faith in the American people and the great American experiment in self-governance and democracy," Biden said on X.

JOE BIDEN'S CANCER HAS SPREAD FURTHER, LEAVING HIM IN 'VERY PAINFUL' CONDITION, HUNTER REVEALS

The former president was diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that had spread to his bones in May 2025, which he said has not stopped him but has sometimes slowed him down.

"While writing the book, I was diagnosed with cancer, a disease known all too well to millions of Americans and their families. My doctors continue to be encouraged by how I've responded to treatment. And the prayers and kind words and well wishes from so many of you have meant more to me and Jill and our family than you can ever know," Biden said.

"Some days are better than others. It hasn't stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down. What that means is, unfortunately, I won’t be able to do as many conversations about my book as I’d hoped. However, I’m hopeful the words on the page speak for themselves," he continued.

Biden recalled his father telling him, "When you get knocked down, get up."

"It's a good lesson for me. And for America," Biden said.

BIDEN CONSPICUOUSLY ABSENT FROM CAMPAIGN TRAIL AS OBAMA, HARRIS STEP UP FOR MIDTERM PUSH

"We are blessed. America is the most unique nation on earth. Unlike other countries, we're built on an idea. An idea bigger than any ocean. More powerful than any army. Stronger than any tyrant or dictator. That idea? All of us are created equal," he added.

item.title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making Dana White press secretary
item.description: Trump says he was joking when he offered Dana White the press secretary job, but confirmed the UFC boss is visiting the White House on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Sunday he was joking when he announced on social media that he had offered UFC boss Dana White the White House press secretary job and lined up a roster of fighters to serve as his assistants.

"I will tell you, I was only kidding," Trump said when asked what prompted the pitch and whether he was serious.

Trump pointed to the fighters he had named as White’s would-be assistants, saying the lineup should have given the joke away. "And you see a lot of rough faces there," he said. 

He also joked that some of the fighters came from "parts unknown."

DANA WHITE DENIES AMERICA 250 UFC FIGHT AT WHITE HOUSE WILL BE 'POLITICAL,' 'NOT AT ALL' ABOUT POLITICS

Trump said he thought White liked the idea and called him "a very capable guy." As for how the UFC boss might handle the job, Trump said, "You wouldn’t mess around with him so much."

"But Dana is actually coming tomorrow," Trump said. He explained that the visit was for other reasons, saying he believed White already planned to be in Washington and would stop by to see him.

TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY OUT OF THE JOB JUST DAYS AFTER ROCKY DEBUT

Trump said some people took to the idea after he floated it. "And then people said, you know, that’s actually a pretty good idea," he said.

The clarification came a day after Trump wrote on Truth Social that he had offered White the job. His post named UFC stars including Khabib Nurmagomedov, Islam Makhachev, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and Amanda Nunes as prospective assistants.

UFC STARS VISIT OVAL OFFICE, THANK PRESIDENT TRUMP FOR TRANSFORMING THE SPORT WITH HISTORIC WHITE HOUSE FIGHT

"Dana, please take the job!" Trump wrote.

White shared Trump’s post on his Instagram Story, along with a photo of himself behind the White House podium. He captioned the photo, "On to the next chapter."

LEAVITT OPENS UP ON HELPING TRUMP FIND NEW PRESS SECRETARY AFTER ZACHARIA DEBACLE: 'WAS NOT FOR HER'

The exchange came weeks after Katie Zacharia’s departure as press secretary. Zacharia had been tapped to succeed Karoline Leavitt, who left in August. Asked Oct. 23 about finding a replacement, Trump told reporters, "We’re in no rush."

Trump and White have known each other for decades, dating back to the UFC’s early years, when Trump hosted fights at his Atlantic City property. White introduced Trump at the 2024 Republican National Convention and joined him on the White House South Lawn in June for UFC Freedom 250.

KAROLINE LEAVITT REVEALS SHE’S ADVISED TRUMP ON WHITE HOUSE REPLACEMENT IN FINAL INTERVIEW AS PRESS SECRETARY

White previously told Sports Business Journal in November 2024 that he had "no personal political aspirations" when asked about a possible role in Trump’s incoming administration.

item.title: Fantasy football managers fume as Ladd McConkey's pregame injury goes unreported until after kickoff
item.description: Ladd McConkey's back spasms during pregame warmups went unreported until after kickoff, leaving fantasy football managers locked in with no warning.
item.content:encoded:
Fantasy football managers who started Ladd McConkey on Sunday got an injury update they probably would have appreciated a little earlier. Preferably, while they could still do something about it.

The Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver was suddenly listed as questionable with a back injury after Sunday's game against the Houston Texans had started. Then came the particularly frustrating news: According to multiple reports, McConkey experienced back spasms during pregame warmups.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Pregame. As in, before the game.

The Chargers' announcement was posted at 4:17 p.m. ET, roughly 12 minutes after the game started.

McConkey wasn't on the team's Friday injury report, and he wasn't among the players declared inactive Sunday. Managers who checked those updates had no warning there that a back problem might interfere with his afternoon.

By the time the questionable designation arrived, managers whose lineups had locked could only wait for another update and hope for the best.

Judging by the reaction on social media, they weren't particularly interested in being patient.

One social media user argued that managers counting on McConkey had every reason to be upset that his "back spasms weren’t communicated to the public before kickoff."

Another called for an investigation into the Chargers' handling of the injury information. Others were simply fed up with having McConkey in their lineups.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

One frustrated fantasy manager complained that McConkey "has ruined my fantasy week 60% of the time this year."

Those were among the responses we can actually print on this website.

To be fair, if you were counting on McConkey to win your fantasy matchup, your team is probably already in trouble (mine included). The Chargers' offense has been a complete dumpster fire, and McConkey hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard.

Los Angeles entered Sunday 0-7 and without an offensive touchdown in its past nine quarters. McConkey had just 17 catches for 286 yards and one touchdown in six appearances, having already missed a game due to injury.

His four catches for 86 yards against the Rams the previous week had at least given managers some reason to feel better about putting him back in their lineups. However, 54 of those yards came on a fluky deflected Hail Mary at the end of the first half.

Even a questionable designation before the game would have given managers with another available receiver a choice. McConkey did not have a target in the first half against the Texans.

It's fair to ask when the Chargers first knew McConkey's back might keep him out and why that information didn't reach the public sooner. The timing of the announcement deserves an explanation, regardless of how much McConkey ultimately plays.

The American Gaming Association put its forecast for legal NFL betting at $29.5 billion this season, counting wagers at regulated U.S. commercial sportsbooks.

People placing those bets, trading through prediction markets and paying to enter fantasy contests are all making decisions with real money. Timely, accurate injury information is a basic requirement, and the NFL needs to make sure its teams provide it while people can still act on it.

Finding out after kickoff that a player was hurt before the game is infuriating. For a league with billions of dollars riding on its games, it's also unacceptable.

item.title: Trump’s proposed Russia deal raises NATO alarm as ex-commander warns Putin seeks influence over Europe
item.description: President Donald Trump says a Russia deal could involve "all of Europe" as retired Gen. Philip Breedlove warns Putin wants spheres of influence.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's push for a deal with Russia to end the war in Ukraine and potentially reshape European security has raised alarm among NATO allies, with a former top alliance commander warning Fox News Digital that President Vladimir Putin has long sought to divide the world into competing spheres of influence.

The warning came as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also appeared to reject what he called a potential "Yalta 2.0," and NATO allies debated direct outreach to Putin ahead of delegations preparing for talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11.

Retired Gen. Philip Breedlove, the former Supreme Allied Commander Europe, warned that Putin's ambitions extend far beyond Ukraine and reflect a broader vision for how global powers should divide influence.

"Putin has a plan for the world, and he has pushed that plan on leaders several times," Breedlove warned before adding: "He talks about it and he writes about it."

ZELENSKYY TO SEEK OFFRAMP FOR YEARS-LONG RUSSIA WAR IN UN SPEECH AFTER TRUMP REVEALS PEACE DEAL IS CLOSE

Trump had suggested Thursday that an agreement with Moscow could extend beyond ending Russia's nearly five-year war in Ukraine.

"It's going to be a big agreement, and it's going to involve more than Ukraine... I could even say it might involve all of Europe," Trump told reporters after meeting Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House.

"It's going to be a big, beautiful agreement, and everyone's going to be thrilled," Trump added.

Breedlove said Putin has repeatedly promoted a vision of dividing global power among Russia, China and the United States.

"The plan is three spheres of influence whereby China controls the Far East, Russia controls Europe, and America controls the Western Hemisphere. I do not expect there's going to be a lot of cooperation from the countries of Europe," he said.

"The Western world is waiting to see what this big plan is, and they are very concerned because it is about them," Breedlove added.

Zelenskyy also warned Friday against repeating the 1945 Yalta Conference, where Allied leaders negotiated Europe's postwar order before the Soviet Union consolidated control over Eastern Europe.

"We don't want to have Yalta 2.0," the Ukrainian leader told CNN. "We don't want to be divided by Russia," he said before adding: "For me, it's not simple and it can be dangerous."

On Sunday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters that discussions on how Europe would look after the Ukraine war were already underway.

"It's one of the key topics that's been raised repeatedly in every conversation, anytime negotiations have been discussed," he said ahead of traveling to Paris for the G7 meeting.

RUBIO SOUNDS CAMPAIGN-READY AS HE RAILS AGAINST OPEN BORDERS, GLOBALISM IN SPEECH FROM ANCIENT GREEK RUINS

"So I think that's what the president is alluding to, is that there's been some advances made and what that architecture could look like post-conflict. We obviously have to get past the conflict to get to that point," he added, clarifying Trump's comments.

Breedlove, however, questioned whether European governments and Ukraine would even accept a broader agreement negotiated without their involvement.

"I do expect that when we get a peek under the hood of what Mr. Putin and Mr. Trump have devised that there may be European partners and allies to include Ukraine that may or may not be enthralled with the proposed solution."

"We have always said nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine," the expert said.

"Neither have we heard anything about the EU or NATO being in this conversation. And yet the EU, NATO and Ukraine are central and the heart of the matter that apparently is going to be discussed."

Tensions also appeared to mount further after Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a rare 90-minute telephone conversation with Putin on Oct. 27, according to reports.

TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen criticized the separate European diplomatic initiatives.

"I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo," she said as Breedlove went on to defend the outreach.

"The two calls that recently took place between Northern leaders in the NATO alliance and Russia, I don't think that they're out of place at all," he said. "I think they're entirely appropriate."

"The great powers of Europe are getting very concerned that someone is dealing with their security without including them in the conversation," he added.

Meanwhile, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot confirmed Sunday that France would participate in the Abu Dhabi negotiations.

"The Europeans will be well represented; France will be in Abu Dhabi to take part in these discussions," Barrot said, according to Reuters.

FORMER UK PRIME MINISTER TONY BLAIR WARNS EUROPE ‘WE DON’T WIN’ IN WAR WITHOUT US SUPPORT

Breedlove warned that any agreement requiring European nations to sacrifice their security to satisfy Moscow would still face fierce resistance.

"If the maximalist demands of Russia remain intact and in order to find peace, all the rest of Europe has to give up its security, sacrifice its security, make itself more susceptible to Russian attack, then this is not going to go well," he said.

"Putin has never been a partner for peace in Ukraine. Putin is not now a partner for peace in Ukraine."

"The EU nations, the NATO nations, and Ukraine are not going to sign up to a plan that suggests that Russia will be able to once again amass its armies, march across borders and intervene in its neighbors' internal business."

"We need to understand that we are in a war. Mr. Putin is at war with the West," he warned.

item.title: Family trapped by powerful floodwaters until 2 neighbors grab a kayak and paddleboard
item.description: As rising floodwaters trapped a mother and a son in their home in Palm Bay, Florida, two neighborhood boys nearby used a kayak and a paddleboard to come to the rescue.
item.content:encoded:
After heavy rainfall caused severe flooding that trapped a desperate Florida family inside their home for hours, two neighborhood brothers with a paddleboard and kayak took dramatic action to do what they could to help. 

The rescue of a mother and son, plus their three dogs, took place Monday in Palm Bay, a city in Brevard County roughly 70 miles southeast of Orlando, as heavy rain flooded homes and streets across the area.

Brittany Grant, a Palm Bay resident, told ClickOrlando that floodwaters began pouring into her home — which forced her and her young son to climb onto the kitchen counter to dodge the rising water, she said.

ALLIGATOR ATTACK ON FLORIDA MOM SPARKS PANICKED 911 CALL: 'HER ARM IS GONE'

But with water continuing to rise, Grant called 911 to no avail, according to reports.

After Grant and her son remained stranded on the counter for hours, she decided to turn to Facebook to plead for help.

Her post caught the attention of a neighborhood mother — whose teenage sons, Lucas Marshall, 17, and Jonah Marshall, 15, set out to rescue the family using just a borrowed kayak and a paddleboard.

MOM OF 2 WHO DIED RESCUING SONS DURING BAHAMAS SNORKELING TRIP IS IDENTIFIED

Jonah Marshall told ClickOrlando he didn't think twice about helping another family.

"Because they needed help, and they were in trouble and danger, so [I] just didn’t think about it and just went to help them," the teen said.

Lucas Marshall described the rescue as "nerve-wracking a little bit," but said he tried to keep Grant's son calm by striking up a conversation.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"It was good because, like, we’re physical and able to do it, so [we] might as well," he said.

"So I was just asking him, like, ‘OK, what’s your name?’" Lucas Marshall added. 

"I was like, ‘How’s school going?’ I was like, ‘This is a weird day, isn’t it?’"

The stranded mom said that she was extremely grateful for her neighbors' help.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"The community came together and saved us," Grant said, according to ClickOrlando. "If it wasn’t for them, I don’t know how we would have gotten out."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Fox News Digital reached out to Grant for comment.

The flooding in Palm Bay also turned deadly Monday, when 34-year-old Joshua Bennett died after his vehicle became trapped in rising floodwaters.

His wife, Stacy Petit Bennett, told WESH 2 News he called her on FaceTime as water surrounded his vehicle.

"He called me on FaceTime, and he was just crying, like, 'I don't know what to do, I don't know what to do,'" she said.

item.title: Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb involved in wild catch-and-run fumble that sums up today's action
item.description: CeeDee Lamb's 10-catch, 195-yard masterclass against the Indianapolis Colts was nearly undone by a stunning fourth-quarter fumble in the red zone.
item.content:encoded:
If you have Dallas Cowboys superstar wide receiver CeeDee Lamb on your fantasy football team, congratulations (also, I hate you).

The standout pass catcher has been crushing it so far this season, sitting in the top three among all NFL wide receivers in receptions (60), yards (709), and touchdown grabs (six).

Sunday was another banner day for the five-time Pro Bowl selection, hauling in 10 catches for 195 yards and a score and proving to everyone why he is one of the best weapons in the league.

TIPS FOR YOUR FANTASY FOOTBALL DRAFT: HOW TO BUILD A WINNING TEAM WITHOUT OVERTHINKING IT

But it wasn't all sunshine and rainbows for Lamb, for as much as he helped America's Team to a victory over the Indianapolis Colts this afternoon, he had a pretty massive blunder at a critical point in the fourth quarter of the game.

Hanging onto a three-point lead and facing a third-and-12 from their own 39-yard-line, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott tossed up a prayer to his dynamic WR1 while staring down the barrel of a blitz.

Lamb plucked the ball mere inches from the ground and proceeded to stand up and run for another 25 yards.

Seems like a clutch play from a clutch player in a high leverage situation, right?

NFL STARS GO ABOVE AND BEYOND TO MAKE INCREDIBLE CATCHES DURING SUNDAY'S WEEK 5 ACTION

Watch the whole thing.

Poor CeeDee did everything right and got his team from a nearly certain punting scenario to the red zone, only to cough it all up and give the Colts a huge shot in the arm.

And for those of you wondering if Indy linebacker Austin Ajiake was the one who tripped Lamb up, thus negating the fumble by way of the ground causing it as a result of a tackle, the play was reviewed and upheld.

Colts ball, and a rare blemish on an otherwise stellar day for CeeDee.

As I mentioned, the Cowboys would end up taking the win on the road in a back-and-forth 27-23 affair, but for a moment there, it looked like CeeDee Lamb went from GOAT to sacrificial lamb in just one wacky play.

item.title: More proof that any team trading for Daniel Jones at the NFL trade deadline is chasing fool's gold
item.description: Daniel Jones threw a game-sealing interception as the Indianapolis Colts fell 27-23 to Dallas, raising major questions ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
The next thing you'll hear about Daniel Jones is how the Minnesota Vikings or some other team is interested in trading for him before the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday.

And the logical question a wise general manager in desperate need of a solid quarterback should be asking is: Why Daniel Jones?

Why that guy?

MINNESOTA VIKINGS' SOFT BENCHING OF KYLER MURRAY LEADS TO CARSON WENTZ TAKING OVER AS NEW STARTING QB

Jones plays for the Indianapolis Colts now and continues to be one of the most disappointing and under-performing reasons that team has been in garage sale mode for nearly a month, as losses increased and optimism dropped off the table.

The Colts lost again on Sunday, this time 27-23 to the Dallas Cowboys, and the way this game went is a testament to why Jones is fools gold at the trade deadline.

SHANE STEICHEN SAYS DANIEL JONES WON'T BE BENCHED BUT COACH AND GENERAL MANAGER CHRIS BALLARD ARE IN TROUBLE

Jones threw an interception on the Colts' final offensive play to seal their loss.

Before that misbegotten pass, he threw an incompletion. Before that, he had an intentional grounding. And he had an incompletion before that.

The Colts had the football with 1:08 to play and needed to score a touchdown and pull out a victory. But that wasn't Dan Marino or Dan Fouts playing for the Colts.

That was Daniel Jones, who, rather than comeback wins, had mostly delivered ways to lose and disappointment during his time with the Indy and the New York Giants before that.

"Didn't finish the way we want to finish," Colts embattled head coach Shane Steichen said afterward.

Of course not, coach, your quarterback is Daniel Jones to whom you committed last season as your starter before he got hurt and crashed your season. You quarterback is Daniel Jones to whom you also committed to this year before he remained healthy and still freakin' helped crash your now 2-7 season.

Steichen will probably be fired at the end of the season for his grand commitment. And there's no telling what the next new general manager and head coach will do with Jones.

COLTS FACE QUARTERBACK UNCERTAINTY AS DANIEL JONES RECOVERS FROM ACHILLES INJURY

But that's only if Jones is still in Indy after the 4 p.m. Tuesday trade deadline.

The Minnesota Vikings reached out to the Colts in recent days about acquiring Jones.

That is significant proof that the Vikings have great confidence in their reputation for developing quarterbacks but are equally tone-deaf about their reputation for making massive mistakes in deciding what quarterbacks they want on their roster.

THE WEEK OF THE BACKUP QB IN THE NFL KICKS OFF AS SANDERS, MILTON, MINSHEW, LOCK, AND WENTZ START

The idea the Vikings or any other team might think Jones is a solution to a quarterback problem rather than a multiplication of a problem is curious. Because it forgets Jones' history of failing.

Jones threw an interception this game, and it marked the fourth consecutive game he's done that. Indeed, he's had only one game this season in which he has not thrown an interception.

And, to be fair, Jones has generally accepted responsibility for his mistakes and his role on an offense that needs to play better.

But there was a moment on Sunday when Jones seemed to blame the uncertain situation the Colts find themselves in with the deadline approaching as a reason the club's collective performance hasn't been as good as expected.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"There's been so much stuff going on and distractions and different things, and we've got to do a better job handling it as a team, collectively executing together, as a group," Jones said.

Wait.

The reason there has been so much "stuff going on" is because the club, led by Jones, has been playing poorly, which led management to begin considering the makeup of the team next year rather than the rest of this year.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

If Jones played better and the Colts won more, there wouldn't be "so much stuff going on," other than winning games.

"... We got to do a good job executing together," Jones said.

True. Jones may get a chance to do that on another team that will see him as improving their situation – kind of like the Colts did before this season began.
